comparisons.peer_topic: Unrecognized Compensation Cost for Unvested Awards
comparisons.peer_summary: Total unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested stock awards was $1.1 billion at December 31, 2024, expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 1.7 years.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup disclose the total unrecognized compensation cost for share-based awards and the estimated period over which that cost will be recognized. However, the magnitude and recognition period differ significantly. Bank of America reported $4.3 billion in unrecognized compensation cost to be recognized over up to four years (weighted-average 2.4 years), whereas Citigroup reported a substantially smaller amount of $1.1 billion to be recognized over a shorter weighted-average period of 1.7 years. comparisons.peer_topic: Employee share-based compensation expense recognition and unamortized costs
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm recognized noncash compensation expense for employee share-based incentive plans in its Consolidated statements of income. At December 31, 2024, approximately $963 million (pretax) of compensation expense for unvested awards remained unamortized and is expected to be amortized over a weighted-average period of 1.6 years, with no such costs capitalized.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase disclose the amount of unrecognized compensation cost for unvested share-based awards as of year-end and the weighted-average period over which it will be amortized. JPMorgan's unrecognized cost ($963 million) is significantly lower than Bank of America's ($4.3 billion), and JPMorgan's amortization period (1.6 years) is shorter than Bank of America's (2.4 years). Additionally, JPMorgan explicitly states it does not capitalize such expenses, a detail not present in the cited Bank of America sentence.
